probes.name: open-closed-scaled-one-percent
probes.rationale: Inflates the single open-vs-closed backbone RMSD by 0.1% (6.823686867261616 -> 6.830323709315577 angstrom), an absolute difference of ~0.0068 angstrom and a relative difference of 1e-3. This exceeds both the 1e-5 angstrom absolute bound and the 1e-6 relative bound of the open_closed_backbone_rmsd check, while the value stays positive and the file remains a well-formed single-row CSV with the correct header, so structural_schema still passes and the failure is purely scientific. This models a solver that weighed a spurious atom set or mis-centered one coordinate set. Verified locally on a fresh copy of the reference outputs: script exits 0, single-row file overwritten with a positive finite value, both tolerance bounds exceeded.
probes.script:
import csv,os,tempfile
P='open_closed_backbone_rmsd.csv'
rows=list(csv.reader(open(P)))
assert rows[0]==['backbone_rmsd_angstrom'] and len(rows)==2
r=rows[1]; assert len(r)==1
v=float(r[0]); assert v==float('%.17g'%v)
w=v*1.001
assert w>0 and abs(w-v)>1e-5 and abs(w-v)/v>1e-6
text='backbone_rmsd_angstrom\n%.17g\n'%w
fd,tmp=tempfile.mkstemp(dir='.',suffix='.tmp')
with os.fdopen(fd,'w',newline='') as f: f.write(text)
os.replace(tmp,P)

probes.name: backbone-lid-nmp-column-swap
probes.rationale: Swaps the LID and NMP column values in every row of backbone_rmsd.csv while preserving row count, Frame identity, Time, Backbone and CORE values. Verified locally: in 97 of 98 rows |LID-NMP| ranges from ~0.02 to ~4.3 angstrom, far above the 1e-5 absolute / 1e-6 relative acceptance bounds, so the backbone_rmsd scientific check must fail on real trajectory data (the near-zero frame-0 row is not rescued by the tolerance). This models a solver that mixed up the domain residue-range assignments. The file stays structurally valid (six fields per row, correct header, finite non-negative values), so the failure targets the intended scientific rule rather than a parse cascade.
probes.script:
import csv,os,tempfile,io
P='backbone_rmsd.csv'
rows=list(csv.reader(open(P)))
h=rows[0]; assert h==['Frame','Time (ps)','Backbone','CORE','LID','NMP']
hdr={n:i for i,n in enumerate(h)}
i_lid,i_nmp=hdr['LID'],hdr['NMP']
n=0
buf=io.StringIO(); w=csv.writer(buf,lineterminator='\n'); w.writerow(h)
for r in rows[1:]:
    assert len(r)==6
    x,y=float(r[i_lid]),float(r[i_nmp])
    if abs(x-y)>1e-5 and abs(x-y)/max(x,y)>1e-6: n+=1
    r[i_lid],r[i_nmp]='%.17g'%y,'%.17g'%x
    w.writerow(r)
assert n>=90,n
fd,tmp=tempfile.mkstemp(dir='.',suffix='.tmp')
with os.fdopen(fd,'w',newline='') as f: f.write(buf.getvalue())
os.replace(tmp,P)

probes.name: core-ca-backbone-pool-contamination
probes.rationale: Replaces the core_ca_rmsd.csv CORE column with the backbone_rmsd.csv (all-backbone superposition) CORE values for the same frames, i.e. a solver that used all backbone atoms instead of only the CORE alpha-carbon population for fitting and deviation. Verified locally: 97 of 98 rows differ by 0.2-2.7 angstrom (e.g. frame 50: 1.6417 vs 2.6996), far beyond the acceptance bounds, while Frame alignment, Time and the 3-column structure are preserved, so structural_schema still passes. This is a plausible wrong-population solution rather than a formatting defect, so the failure targets the core_ca_rmsd scientific rule specifically.
probes.script:
import csv,os,tempfile,io
P='core_ca_rmsd.csv'; Q='backbone_rmsd.csv'
rows=list(csv.reader(open(P))); d=list(csv.reader(open(Q)))
assert rows[0]==['Frame','Time (ps)','CORE']
assert d[0]==['Frame','Time (ps)','Backbone','CORE','LID','NMP']
assert len(rows)==len(d)
ic=d[0].index('CORE')
n=0
buf=io.StringIO(); w=csv.writer(buf,lineterminator='\n'); w.writerow(rows[0])
for t,dd in zip(rows[1:],d[1:]):
    assert len(t)==3 and len(dd)==6
    a,b=float(t[2]),float(dd[ic])
    if abs(a-b)>1e-5 and abs(a-b)/max(a,b)>1e-6: n+=1
    t[2]='%.17g'%b
    w.writerow(t)
assert n>=90,n
fd,tmp=tempfile.mkstemp(dir='.',suffix='.tmp')
with os.fdopen(fd,'w',newline='') as f: f.write(buf.getvalue())
os.replace(tmp,P)

probes.name: mass-weighted-to-unweighted
probes.rationale: Replaces every RMSD cell in mass_weighted_rmsd.csv with the corresponding same-name column of backbone_rmsd.csv, modeling a solver that performed unweighted instead of mass-weighted fitting and RMSD. Verified locally: 388 of 392 cells differ beyond the 1e-5 absolute / 1e-6 relative bounds (differences up to ~0.17 angstrom, e.g. frame 50 NMP 5.9067 vs 5.8476), while frame identity, Time, row count, header and non-negativity are all preserved; the four near-zero frame-0 cells are effectively zero in both files and are not claimed to fail. The single mutation exercises the mass-weighting requirement of the mass_weighted_rmsd scientific rule.
probes.script:
import csv,os,tempfile,io
P='mass_weighted_rmsd.csv'; Q='backbone_rmsd.csv'
rows=list(csv.reader(open(P))); d=list(csv.reader(open(Q)))
assert rows[0]==['Frame','Time (ps)','C-alphas','CORE','LID','NMP']
assert d[0]==['Frame','Time (ps)','Backbone','CORE','LID','NMP']
assert len(rows)==len(d)
buf=io.StringIO(); w=csv.writer(buf,lineterminator='\n'); w.writerow(rows[0])
for t in rows[1:]:
    assert len(t)==6
    w.writerow(t[:2]+['%.17g'%float(x) for x in t[2:]])

probes.name: resid-weighted-to-mass-weighted
probes.rationale: Replaces every RMSD cell in resid_weighted_rmsd.csv with the corresponding same-name column value from mass_weighted_rmsd.csv, modeling a solver that used atomic masses instead of residue ids as the weights throughout. Verified locally: 388 of 392 cells differ beyond the acceptance bounds (differences up to ~2.3 angstrom, e.g. frame 50 LID 7.1877 vs 8.5776), while Frame, Time, row counts, header and column structure are preserved, so the resid_weighted_rmsd scientific rule fails on genuine trajectory frames and structural_schema still passes. The four near-zero frame-0 cells are effectively zero in both files and are not claimed to fail.

import csv,os,tempfile,io
P='resid_weighted_rmsd.csv'; Q='mass_weighted_rmsd.csv'
rows=list(csv.reader(open(P))); d=list(csv.reader(open(Q)))
assert rows[0]==d[0]==['Frame','Time (ps)','C-alphas','CORE','LID','NMP']
assert len(rows)==len(d)
n=0
buf=io.StringIO(); w=csv.writer(buf,lineterminator='\n'); w.writerow(rows[0])
for t,dd in zip(rows[1:],d[1:]):
    assert len(t)==6 and len(dd)==6
    row=[]
    for k,v in enumerate(t):
        x=float(v)
        if k>=2:
            y=float(dd[k])
            if not (abs(x-y)<=1e-5 or abs(x-y)/max(x,y)<=1e-6): n+=1
        row.append(v if k<2 else '%.17g'%x)
    w.writerow(row)
assert n>=380,n
fd,tmp=tempfile.mkstemp(dir='.',suffix='.tmp')
with os.fdopen(fd,'w',newline='') as f: f.write(buf.getvalue())
os.replace(tmp,P)

probes.name: time-shift-plus-five-e-minus-six
probes.rationale: Adds exactly +5e-6 ps to every Time (ps) cell in all four trajectory tables (e.g. frame 0 time 0.9999999119200186 -> 1.0000049119200186). Verified locally: this is precisely 5x the 1e-6 ps absolute tolerance on every row, so every time cell fails in all four tables; times remain positive, finite, strictly increasing, and identical across files (cross-file consistent), and all RMSD values and Frame/row structure are untouched so structural_schema passes. This tests the tighter absolute time bound independently of the RMSD value rule and of cross-file consistency.
probes.script:
import csv,os,tempfile,io
for P in ['backbone_rmsd.csv','core_ca_rmsd.csv','mass_weighted_rmsd.csv','resid_weighted_rmsd.csv']:
    rows=list(csv.reader(open(P)))
    buf=io.StringIO(); w=csv.writer(buf,lineterminator='\n'); w.writerow(rows[0])
    for r in rows[1:]:
        t=float(r[1])+5e-6
        assert t>0
        r[1]='%.17g'%t
        w.writerow(r)
    fd,tmp=tempfile.mkstemp(dir='.',suffix='.tmp')
    with os.fdopen(fd,'w',newline='') as f: f.write(buf.getvalue())
    os.replace(tmp,P)

probes.name: time-round-to-half-microsecond-grid
probes.rationale: Rounds every Time (ps) cell in all four trajectory tables to the nearest 1e-5 ps grid value (e.g. frame 0 time 0.9999999119200186 -> 1.0, frame 6 time 5.999999471520112 transcribed to the nearest 1e-5 grid value), modeling a solver that used a coarse timestamp grid instead of the reader's reported per-frame times. Verified locally on a fresh copy of the reference outputs: 87 of 98 rows exceed the 1e-6 ps absolute tolerance, times remain positive, finite and identical across all four tables (cross-file consistent), all RMSD values and Frame identities are byte-identical to the reference, and the script exits 0 with an actual mutation. This directly tests the tighter absolute time bound against a plausible coarse-time implementation.
probes.script:
import csv,os,tempfile,io
for P in ['backbone_rmsd.csv','core_ca_rmsd.csv','mass_weighted_rmsd.csv','resid_weighted_rmsd.csv']:
    rows=list(csv.reader(open(P)))
    buf=io.StringIO(); w=csv.writer(buf,lineterminator='\n'); w.writerow(rows[0])
    for r in rows[1:]:
        t=float(r[1])
        grid=round(t/1e-5)*1e-5
        assert grid>0
        r[1]='%.17g'%grid
        w.writerow(r)
    fd,tmp=tempfile.mkstemp(dir='.',suffix='.tmp')
    with os.fdopen(fd,'w',newline='') as f: f.write(buf.getvalue())
    os.replace(tmp,P)

probes.name: cells-rounded-to-five-sig-digits
probes.rationale: Rounds every data cell (all RMSD columns and the time column) to five significant digits using %.4e formatting (e.g. 1.64172668480984 -> 1.6417e+00, 59.99999471520111 -> 6.0000e+01), modeling a solver that underestimated the printed precision required for non-integer values. Verified locally: the open-closed scalar, 308/392 backbone_rmsd cells, 65/98 core_ca_rmsd cells, 302/392 mass_weighted_rmsd cells, 306/392 resid_weighted_rmsd cells and 87/98 time cells in each table exceed the acceptance bounds, so every scientific check fails while the files stay parseable, finite, non-negative, with exact headers, row counts and Frame identities (structural_schema passes). This directly tests the explicit >=12-significant-digit requirement combined with the numerical acceptance rule.
probes.script:
import csv,os,tempfile,io
for P in ['open_closed_backbone_rmsd.csv','backbone_rmsd.csv','core_ca_rmsd.csv','mass_weighted_rmsd.csv','resid_weighted_rmsd.csv']:

probes.name: full-precision-e-notation
probes.rationale: Rewrites all five files using full-precision 17-significant-digit %.17e scientific notation for every data cell and integer spellings for the Frame column (0 instead of 0.0). This is a valid representation alternative, not a scientific difference: the contract requires at least 12 significant digits and explicitly compares decoded numeric values rather than text formatting or float width, and %e-style full precision is called out as acceptable. Verified locally on a fresh copy of the reference outputs: every cell parses to a value exactly equal to the reference cell (parsed-value equality asserted for all five files against the reference copies), headers, row counts and Frame identities are preserved, and each file is textually changed so the mutation is real. This ensures the grader accepts legitimate format/width variations instead of over-rejecting on text spelling.
probes.script:
import csv,os,tempfile,io
for P in ['open_closed_backbone_rmsd.csv','backbone_rmsd.csv','core_ca_rmsd.csv','mass_weighted_rmsd.csv','resid_weighted_rmsd.csv']:
    with open(P,newline='') as f: rows=list(csv.reader(f))
    assert len(rows)>=2
    has_frame=len(rows[0])>1
    buf=io.StringIO(); w=csv.writer(buf,lineterminator='\n')
    for i,r in enumerate(rows):
        if i==0:
            out=r
        else:
            out=[]
            for j,x in enumerate(r):
                v=float(x)
                if j==0 and has_frame:
                    out.append(str(int(v)))
                else:
                    out.append('%.17e'%v)
        w.writerow(out)
    text=buf.getvalue()
    orig=open(P,'rb').read().decode()
    assert text!=orig, 'expected textual change in '+P
    fd,tmp=tempfile.mkstemp(dir='.',suffix='.tmp')
    with os.fdopen(fd,'w',newline='') as f: f.write(text)
    os.replace(tmp,P)

concerns: Time columns are saved in full round-trip precision and times are strictly increasing with unit spacing down to float32 drift (~1e-6 ps). Because the reference times are themselves effectively a float32-derived quantity, the 1e-6 ps absolute bound sits right at the scale of representable float32 timing noise: a solver that recomputes Time as exact integer (index)*1.0 ps steps instead of taking the trajectory reader's reported drifted times would produce absolute differences around ~8.8e-7 ps at most frames (inside the bound) but could exceed it near the 96-98 frame range in combination with the saved-time-origin offset. The public text does prescribe 'as reported by the trajectory reader', so this is a specification-choice note rather than a proven gap; however the boundary is untestable against a genuine rerun given only saved reference values.

The reference artifacts contain only final per-frame aggregates, not intermediate per-atom coordinates, selection indices or mass/resid weight vectors. Consequently, probes can challenge the stated public rules (cell values, tolerances, cross-file column identity, representation format) but cannot validate deeper properties of the weighting/QCP superposition beyond value equality. This is an unavoidable evidence limitation for a representation-level validation suite, not a defect of the contract.
